lessons.title: Soil and farming

objectives: Say what soil is made of and name three types of soil.
Explain why loam is the best soil for most crops.
Describe good farming practices and how to stop soil erosion.
reviewNotes: Crop classification (food/cash) is simplified: some crops (banana, maize) are both.

blocks.title: What is soil?
blocks.md: Soil is made of tiny pieces of broken **rock**, **humus** (decayed plants and animals), **air**, **water** and living things such as worms and bacteria. Plants take water and minerals from the soil. Humus makes the soil dark and rich.

blocks.caption: Three types of soil.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: sandy soil has big grains, clay soil has tiny grains, and loam is a mixture of sand, clay and humus.

blocks.title: Types of soil
blocks.md:
- **Sandy soil**: big grains, water passes through quickly, it is dry and poor.
- **Clay soil**: very small grains, sticky when wet, holds a lot of water, water drains slowly.
- **Loam**: a mixture of sand, clay and humus; it holds enough water and air, so it is **best for most crops**.

blocks.title: Good farming
blocks.md: Farmers **clear** the land, **plant** at the right time, **weed**, protect crops from pests and **harvest**. To keep the soil fertile they add **manure or compost**, use **crop rotation** (growing different crops in turn, for example maize then beans), and cover the soil with leaves (**mulching**). Crops can be **food crops** (maize, cassava, plantain) or **cash crops** (cocoa, coffee, cotton, bananas for export).

blocks.title: Soil erosion
blocks.md: **Erosion** is when rain and wind carry the good topsoil away. It happens when trees and grass are cut or burned and the soil is left bare, especially on slopes. To stop it: plant trees and grass, make ridges across the slope, use mulch, and avoid bush burning.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A farmer's soil is sandy and dries quickly. Give two ways to improve it.
steps: Add compost or manure: humus holds water.
Cover the soil with mulch to reduce drying.
blocks.answer: Add compost or manure and use mulch.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Why do farmers grow maize and beans in turn on the same field?
steps: Beans add nutrients to the soil, and maize uses them.
This keeps the soil fertile and reduces some pests and diseases.
blocks.answer: Crop rotation keeps the soil fertile and reduces pests.

objectives: Describe air as a mixture of gases and say what it is used for.
Name the instruments used to measure weather.

reviewNotes: Air composition given as 'about 4/5 nitrogen, 1/5 oxygen' (standard approximation). Seasons of Cameroon are stated in a very general way; regional differences exist. Water treatment advice is general and should be reviewed by a health worker.
The water cycle is in the existing 'Matter and energy' lesson.

blocks.title: Air
blocks.md: **Air** is all around us. It is a **mixture of gases**: about four-fifths **nitrogen** and about one-fifth **oxygen**, with small amounts of carbon dioxide and water vapour. We need oxygen to breathe and fires need it to burn. Air takes up space and moving air is **wind**. Air is not visible, but we can feel wind and see a balloon grow when we blow into it.

blocks.title: Water
blocks.md: Water is used for drinking, cooking, washing and farming. Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water and water vapour (gas). To make water **safe to drink**, boil it, filter it, or treat it as advised by a health worker. Do not drink water from dirty ponds or streams without treating it.

blocks.caption: Weather instruments.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: the thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius, the rain gauge measures rainfall in millimetres and the wind vane shows the wind direction.

blocks.title: Weather and seasons
blocks.md: **Weather** is the state of the air at a place and time: temperature, rainfall, wind, clouds and sunshine. **Climate** is the usual weather over many years. Most of Cameroon has a **dry season** and a **rainy season**, but the length and the details differ from region to region (for example, the north is drier than the south).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that air is empty: it is a mixture of gases.
- Confusing **weather** (today) with **climate** (the usual pattern).
- Reading a thermometer from the wrong end of the liquid: read where the top of the liquid is.
- Saying that boiled water is not needed if the water looks clear: clear water can still carry germs.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: In four days the rain gauge shows 12 mm, 0 mm, 8 mm and 20 mm. Find the total and the mean rainfall per day.
blocks.answer: 40 mm in all; the mean is 10 mm a day.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Which instrument would you use to find which way the wind blows?
steps: The thermometer measures temperature and the rain gauge rainfall.
The wind vane turns to show the direction of the wind.
